text:
Maya: Hey team — customer on Vercel Edge runtime reports streaming responses from our Node TS SDK stop after the first chunk, then the connection just hangs for ~30s and Vercel returns a 502. Works fine in local Node.
Samir: Do we have SDK version and minimal repro? Edge vs Node often surfaces ReadableStream differences. :eyes:
Maya: Using redwood-inference-js@0.5.3 (installed via npm). Repro snippet they gave: 
```ts
const res = await client.chat.completions.create({ model: 'gpt-open-16', input: 'tell me a joke', stream: true })
const reader = res.body.getReader()
while (true) {
  const { done, value } = await reader.read()
  if (done) break
  console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(value))
}
```
It logs one chunk then nothing. No errors in app logs.
Eli: Any proxies or middleware on Vercel? And are they using the Edge Functions (runtime: experimental-edge) or Node Serverless?
Maya: They're on Edge Functions. No custom middleware. Also tried adding `Accept: text/event-stream` and `Cache-Control: no-transform` — no change.
Samir: Known issue: SDK 0.5.x used a Node stream-oriented body that assumes Node's streaming semantics. Edge fetch returns a ReadableStream whose reader behaves slightly differently, and some polyfills cause early cancellation. Two quick asks: can they try upgrading to 0.6.1 (edge-fixes) and share fetch/runtime stack?
Maya: Asked customer to try upgrade. In meantime they shared deploy logs showing many short-lived CONNECT frames then a single data chunk. Logs: 
```
[edge] 2026-02-08T14:11:05Z request id=abc123 stream: chunk 1
[edge] 2026-02-08T14:11:35Z upstream closed, 502
```
Eli: Also check whether Vercel injector is buffering due to `Transfer-Encoding` headers. Some Edge providers will buffer if `content-length` unknown and chunk sizes are tiny. If first chunk < 512 bytes, they might buffer.
Samir: Good point. Another quick repro to try (pure fetch, no SDK) to confirm server-side streaming: 
```ts
const r = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/stream?prompt=hi', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer x' } })
const reader = r.body!.getReader()
for (;;) { const {done, value} = await reader.read(); if (done) break; console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(value)); }
```
If that also stalls, problem is platform or server. If that works, it's SDK-layer.
Maya: Customer tried pure fetch and it streams fine. So SDK is culprit. They also mentioned adding `responseType: 'stream'` in some wrappers — unclear.
Samir: Ok that matches the Node->Edge mismatch hypothesis. Workarounds: 1) Upgrade to 0.6.1 which adds an Edge-aware response body path; 2) If stuck on 0.5.x, use raw fetch as a shim in Edge (we can add small snippet to docs). Which SDK import are they using — `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` or the new modular API?
Maya: They import default `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'`.
Eli: The modular API uses `createEdgeClient` under the hood in >=0.6.1. Also there was a bug where the SDK called `body.getReader()` and then immediately attached a stream transformer that could call `controller.close()` prematurely in some polyfill combos. Fixed in patch.
Maya: Customer upgraded to 0.6.1 and reports streaming now works on Edge. :tada:
Samir: Great — can we mark this as a support KB entry? Add repro and recommended fixes (upgrade, temp raw-fetch shim, ensure small-chunk coalescing).
Maya: I'll create a KB. Draft notes: 1) Symptoms: single chunk then hang on Edge runtime; 2) Likely cause: SDK Node-stream path incompatible with Edge ReadableStream; 3) Workarounds: upgrade to 0.6.1, or replace SDK streaming call with raw fetch loop; 4) If still failing: capture network HAR and edge logs and we can escalate.
deploy-bot: Deployed support KB draft to staff-only repo (link: https://git.redwood/supp-kb/edge-streaming).
Eli: Also flag engineering to add an automatic detection in SDK to throw a clear error if used in Edge with an old version — reduce user confusion.
Samir: Filed ENG issue #INF-4822 for edge-detection + better error.
Maya: Closing loop with customer and adding KB link. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
